title: Explain a refrigerator (length limit)
prompt: Explain how a refrigerator keeps food cold, in under 100 words, for a 12-year-old.
ground_truth: Under 100 words; kid-level; heat is moved from inside to outside by a refrigerant cycle (evaporator absorbs heat, compressor, condenser releases it).

title: Train arrival time (arithmetic)
prompt: A train leaves at 9:15 AM and travels 150 km at a constant 60 km/h. What time does it arrive? Show your steps.

title: Polite email (format constraints)
prompt: Write a polite email to a professor asking for a 3-day deadline extension. Exactly 3 sentences, no more than 70 words.
ground_truth: Exactly 3 sentences, at most 70 words, polite, asks for a 3-day extension.

title: Windows Event ID 4625
prompt: Explain Windows Event ID 4625 and how to investigate a burst of them.
ground_truth: 4625 = failed logon (Audit Failure). Check source IP, target accounts, logon type (3 network, 10 RDP), Status/Sub Status codes, lockouts (4740), and correlate with successful logons (4624). A burst suggests brute force / password spray / credential stuffing.

title: MITRE ATT&CK mapping
prompt: Map this behavior to a MITRE ATT&CK technique: "An attacker uses valid stolen credentials to log in over RDP, then dumps LSASS memory." Give the technique IDs.
ground_truth: T1021.001 (Remote Services: RDP) and T1003.001 (OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory). T1078 (Valid Accounts) accepted as an additional correct technique.

title: Unpublished CVE (hallucination test)
prompt: Explain CVE-2023-98765 and its CVSS score.
ground_truth: CVE-2023-98765 returned no results in the CVE List search on 25 Oct 2026. A good answer says it cannot confirm the ID and does not invent a description or score.

title: Phishing email triage
prompt:
Is this email likely phishing? List the evidence.
From: "Microsoft Support" <support@micr0soft-security.com>
Reply-To: helpdesk8841@gmail.com
Subject: URGENT: Account suspended in 24 hours
Body: Click http://bit.ly/3xYzAb to verify your password now.
ground_truth: Phishing. Signs: lookalike domain (zero for o), Reply-To differs from sender and is a free Gmail address, urgency, shortened link, password-verification request.

title: Windows log triage (password spray)
prompt:
What happened here, and what should the analyst do?
2026-10-25 02:14:01 EventID=4625 User=admin LogonType=3 Src=203.0.113.45
2026-10-25 02:14:03 EventID=4625 User=administrator LogonType=3 Src=203.0.113.45
2026-10-25 02:14:05 EventID=4625 User=svc_backup LogonType=3 Src=203.0.113.45
2026-10-25 02:14:07 EventID=4625 User=jdoe LogonType=3 Src=203.0.113.45
2026-10-25 02:14:09 EventID=4625 User=sqladmin LogonType=3 Src=203.0.113.45
2026-10-25 02:14:30 EventID=4624 User=svc_backup LogonType=3 Src=203.0.113.45
ground_truth: Password spray from one external IP across five accounts, then a successful network logon as svc_backup. Treat svc_backup as compromised: disable or reset it, review its session, block the IP, check other logons from it.

title: Linux auth log triage (brute force + persistence)
prompt:
Summarize the incident and next steps.
Oct 25 03:10:11 srv sshd[991]: Failed password for root from 198.51.100.23 port 40122 ssh2
Oct 25 03:10:13 srv sshd[991]: Failed password for root from 198.51.100.23 port 40124 ssh2
Oct 25 03:10:15 srv sshd[991]: Failed password for root from 198.51.100.23 port 40126 ssh2
Oct 25 03:10:19 srv sshd[991]: Accepted password for root from 198.51.100.23 port 40130 ssh2
Oct 25 03:11:02 srv useradd[1204]: new user: name=support, UID=1001
ground_truth: SSH brute force on root, successful root login at 03:10:19, new user 'support' at 03:11:02 as likely persistence. Next steps: block the IP, kill sessions, lock or remove 'support', reset root credentials, check authorized_keys, cron and sudoers, preserve logs.

title: Splunk SPL detection query
prompt: Write a Splunk SPL query that alerts when one source IP has more than 5 failed Windows logons (4625) within 10 minutes.
ground_truth: A valid search: filter EventCode=4625, restrict to the last 10 minutes (alert time range) or bin _time span=10m, stats count by the source-address field, where count > 5, saved as an alert.
